That makes this a real guard bypass with no demonstrated exfiltration channel, so high rather than critical.

reason: The failure as stated cannot happen. _claim_sentences keeps the [n] markers inside the claim string (citecheck.py:108-122), so a duplicated sentence citing DIFFERENT sources is a different string, and cleaned.replace(sentence, ..., 1) (citecheck.py:273) cannot land on the other occurrence. A collision needs byte-identical text AND identical markers. At that point the two claims have the same content and the same sources, so which copy gets softened carries no honesty inversion, only audit-verdict noise.
evidence_checked: Read _claim_sentences and the softening loop, then ran _claim_sentences on the raw finding's scenario in the sidecar venv.
repro_check: sidecar/.venv/bin/python: _claim_sentences('- Revenue rose 12% in FY24 [1].\n\nBody text. Revenue rose 12% in FY24 [2].', 2, srcs) -> two claims '...[1].' and '...[2].'. md.count('Revenue rose 12% in FY24 [2].') == 1, so the replace can only hit its own occurrence.
